correctness.rationale: For every nonzero real column and every nonzero orthogonal data-noise component, direct residual decomposition proves alpha_R(k)=lambda^{-1}(1+q/e_k^2), warm error e_1=-q/e_0 and the nonvanishing delayed error recurrence e_(k+1)=-q e_k/e_(k-1)^2. Taking logarithms gives an exactly solved linear recurrence with modulus-sqrt(2) complex characteristic roots. The angle is irrational relative to pi because 2cos(theta)=1/sqrt(2) is not an algebraic integer, so phase density gives both positive- and negative-infinite subsequences except at balanced u_0=0, where signs alternate with fixed magnitude. RD uses difference r_1-r_0=-a(e_1-e_0), thus its second scalar step equals 1/lambda and e_2=0. No zero denominator occurs before termination; the z=0 consistency boundary solves on step one. Every quantifier is within the one-unknown exact-arithmetic stated domain. `verify.py` additionally passed 1457 exact-rational assertions; finite checks do not prove the infinite limsup/liminf.

originality.rationale: The claimed effect is not the known recurrence u_(k+1)=u_k-2u_(k-1), the known irrational phase, nor the known one-step false cycle. The source manuscript derives that recurrence only for two positive singular modes under consistent Ax=b. For a fixed nullspace-of-transpose residual it does not address the singular-mode boundary: the entire least-squares error has nonzero bounded two-cycle or unbounded excursions rather than convergence, while the matching residual-difference update cancels this residual and terminates on step two. An earlier published one-step undelayed inconsistent map has a bounded false cycle, mathematically different from this delayed all-time classification; published consistent two-mode DR/RD finite-step comparisons do not imply the noisy scalar result. Accessible exact mathematical records and full text establish no dominating result; older unindexed coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: The recurrence, its characteristic roots, and irrational rotation are explicitly derived in Xin Xu (2026); extension to a zero singular mode may be independently familiar to specialists and historical priority is not certain.
A relevant extended-normal-equation paper and an older surrogate-hyperplane paper were accessible only through abstracts/metadata; a hidden equivalent statement in their full text cannot be excluded.
Some older unindexed analyses of lagged surrogate steps on inconsistent data may cover the same exact scalar result.

value.rationale: The question is the first noise-contaminated boundary of a newly proposed practical residual-gradient stepsize pair, not an arbitrary example. The exact one-column full-column-rank case is the smallest dimension that permits nonzero inconsistent data while retaining a unique least-squares minimizer. The result classifies every initialization and noise magnitude into a nonoptimal two-cycle versus recurrent arbitrarily large errors, and at the same initial point the competing residual-difference formula cancels orthogonal noise and terminates exactly. This supplies a meaningful, severe distinction between residual-norm-delayed scaling and secant-difference scaling that is invisible in consistent-system convergence theorems. No recommendation is made for actual floating-point or safeguarded solvers.
